mission.title: Install and Configure Docker Desktop Kubernetes
mission.description: Docker Desktop for Mac provides an integrated Docker experience on macOS, allowing users to run Kubernetes clusters locally. It simplifies the setup process for developers looking to test and develop applications in a Kubernetes environment without the overhead of managing a full cluster. Key trade-offs include limited scalability compared to cloud solutions and potential performance constraints based on local machine resources.

steps.title: Download Docker Desktop
steps.description:
This step involves downloading the Docker Desktop application for macOS, which includes Kubernetes support.

```bash

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

```

> This opens the download page for Docker Desktop.

steps.title: Install Docker Desktop
steps.description:
Run the downloaded installer to install Docker Desktop on your macOS system.

```bash

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

drag Docker to Applications

```

> Replace 'Docker.dmg' with the actual downloaded file name if different.
> This installs Docker Desktop into your Applications folder.

steps.title: Enable Kubernetes
steps.description:
After installation, enable Kubernetes in the Docker Desktop settings to run a local Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

open -a Docker

sleep 10 && open -a Docker --args --enable-kubernetes

```

> Launch Docker Desktop.
> Wait for Docker to start and then enable Kubernetes.

steps.title: Verify Kubernetes Installation
steps.description:
Check that Kubernetes is running correctly by using kubectl to get the nodes.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> This should show the local Kubernetes node in a Ready state.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Docker Desktop
uninstall.description:
This step will remove Docker Desktop and all associated Kubernetes resources, which may lead to data loss.

```bash

open /Applications

rm -rf Docker.app

```

> Navigate to the Applications folder.
> This command removes Docker Desktop from your system.

upgrade.title: Upgrade Docker Desktop
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up any important data. The upgrade process will replace the existing version with the latest.

```bash

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

drag Docker to Applications

```

> Download the latest version from the official site.
> Open the downloaded installer.
> Replace the existing application with the new version.

troubleshooting.title: Kubernetes cluster is not starting
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Insufficient resources allocated to Docker Desktop.

**Fix:**
Increase the CPU and memory allocation in Docker Desktop settings.

troubleshooting.title: kubectl get nodes returns 'No resources found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Kubernetes may not be enabled or started.

**Fix:**
Ensure Kubernetes is enabled in Docker Desktop settings and restart Docker.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubectl: command not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** kubectl is not installed or not in the PATH.

**Fix:**
Install kubectl using 'brew install kubectl' or ensure it's in your PATH.

troubleshooting.title: Docker Desktop fails to start
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Conflicting applications or insufficient permissions.

**Fix:**
Check for conflicting applications and ensure Docker Desktop has the necessary permissions.
